newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-TONY GWYNN TAKES SEVENTH BATTING TITLE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-TONY GWYNN TAKES SEVENTH BATTING TITLE.

text.p: The San Diego Padres' Tony Gwynn won his record-tying seventh National League batting title Sunday despite going hitless in four at-bats and having four more phantom "oh-fers" added for statistical reasons.

On a day when his Padres completed a three-game road sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers to claim the National League West title, Gwynn's brother Chris had the game-winning hit while he went 0-for-4, dropping his season batting average to .353.

With 502 appearances needed to qualify for the batting title, Gwynn had four hitless at-bats added to his total to qualify. That left Gwynn with a .349 average, surpassing outfielder Ellis Burks of the Colorado Rockies with .344.
The seventh batting title tied Gwynn with Hall of Famers Rogers Hornsby and Stan Musial for the N.L. record.
Burks had an amazing season that saw him belt 40 homers and drive in 128 runs while stealing 32 bases, but he did not lead the league in any major category.

His teammate and first baseman Andres Galarraga took a couple of major honours. Galarraga launched a league-best 47 homers and drove in a major-league best 150 runs, the highest total in baseball since Los Angeles Dodger Tommy Davis had 153 in 1962.
Galarraga had previously led the N.L. with a .370 batting average in 1993, and in doubles (42) and hits (184) in 1988 with Montreal.

Rockies second baseman Eric Young's 53 stolen bases were three better than New York Mets centre fielder Lance Johnson's 50. Young's previous career high was 42 in his rookie year of 1993. He led the minors in steals three times in his career.

Johnson was the runaway leader with 227 hits and is the first player in baseball history to lead the National and American League in hits in a season. Johnson paced the A.L. with 186 for the Chicago White Sox last year.

John Smoltz, likely to be voted his first Cy Young Award, headed the N.L. wins and strikeout lists. The right-hander was 24-8 with a 2.94 ERA and 276 strikeouts over 253 2/3 innings. He previously won the 1992 strikeout title with 215.

The Florida Marlins' Kevin Brown, who was 17-11 with 159 strikeouts over 233 innings, won his first career ERA title with a major-league best and career-low 1.89. His previous best was a 3.32 for Texas in 1992 when he led the A.L. in wins (21) and innings pitched (265 2/3). Atlanta's Greg Maddux, who won the last three years, finished second at 2.72.

Los Angeles closer Todd Worrell and Cincinnati's Jeff Brantley both had 44 saves, tying for the major-league lead. Worrell previously led the league as a St Louis Cardinal with 36 in 1986 when he was named Rookie of the Year. It was Brantley's first title.
